PROXIMAL_FAILURE_FROM_THE_§177_RAW_REASO.rowText: A belt conveyor runs in the packing hall and an operative walks the gangway alongside. The fixed guard over the head drum nip point is in position. At this morning's pre-start check the fitter initialled the sheet, which covers belt tracking and lubrication; the fastenings were last torque-checked at the annual service. No tools rest on the guard.

whatTheModelEmitted.quotedEvidenceVerbatim: The fixed guard over the head drum nip point is in position.
whatTheModelEmitted.reasoningVerbatim: The conveyor nip point is a well-known crush/entanglement hazard for a worker walking the adjacent gangway; the observation confirms the guard is currently in place, so this is a controlled hazard rather than an active exposure, but is included as it is a distinct hazard family (conveyors) not separately captured by the machine_guarding finding.
whatTheModelEmitted.explanationVerbatim: The observation reports the head drum nip point guard is currently in place and free of tools, and the pre-start check plus torque-check history is stated as completed, so no additional current gap is established beyond the guarding hazard already found deterministically. A conveyor-specific candidate is added to reflect the nip point exposure the operative walking the gangway would face if the guard were absent, but the stated current condition is that it is fitted, so it is recorded as controlled rather than active. No decision-critical facts are missing and no cross-hazard interaction is established on the facts given.

PROXIMAL_FAILURE_FROM_THE_§177_RAW_REASO.diagnosis: the model treated present physical presence — the guard being in position — as sufficient to settle the guarding state relevant to the decision. Because it believed the state was settled, the temporal question about the annual-service torque check was never reached, and the §176 rule, which lives in the list of things that do not establish a fact, was never consulted on this path.

theDistinctionThisEstablishes.CONTROL_PRESENCE: the control exists and is physically in position
theDistinctionThisEstablishes.CONTROL_PROPERTY_SUFFICIENCY: the property the current decision actually turns on — securement, functional operation, effectiveness, configuration, protective response
theDistinctionThisEstablishes.forHR04: presence / in-position evidence does not by itself establish current securement of the fixed guard. Only once current securement remains unresolved does the temporal sufficiency of the historical torque verification become relevant at all.

whatIsNOTConcluded: that physical presence is generally insufficient — presence may completely establish a presence fact
that visual or physical evidence is generally insufficient
that historical records are generally insufficient
that the model should function-test or reverify by default
PROXIMAL_FAILURE_FROM_THE_§177_RAW_REASO.theNarrowHypothesis: evidence that establishes ONE property of a control must not automatically be treated as establishing a DIFFERENT decision-critical property of that control
